### Opening a PR

Turn a finished, verified branch into small ordered commits and a ready PR with a one-minute body. The main session runs every `git push` and `gh` call; a worker returns a patch, a proposed title and body, and evidence.

1. **Work in a worktree off trunk.** Writing workers already run `isolated: true`; the main session applies their patches in its own worktree. A dirty branch with unrelated work: save the unrelated part as a patch, start a fresh worktree from trunk, apply only what belongs. A snarled worktree: start a fresh one from trunk and redo the change minimally. Run `skill://worktree-cleanup` after parallel runs.
2. **Commit liberally, then shape history before opening.** Each commit is a future PR: landable, ordered to tell the story. Amend when the fix belongs in a just-made commit; make a new commit when it is separable. Commit bodies do not restate the subject. Commit through the eval `commit` namespace (`d = await commit.draft()`, then `await d.commit("subject", ["- body"])`), never `git add` or `git commit`, so only the lines you and your workers wrote are committed.
3. **Strip slop before the commit, then before review.** Run `skill://no-comments` and `skill://unslop` over the diff; the done gate already refuses new comments, and `no-comments` adds the semantic pass the gate cannot do. Write every PR title, description, and commit body with `skill://technical-writing` (every layer except Diátaxis; apply the STE vocabulary rules: one word per action, keep articles, a plain verb over `-ing` where one works), then apply `skill://unslop`.
4. **Title.** Conventional Commits `type(scope): subject`, no trailing period. Type is one of `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`, `perf`. Scope is the area, such as `ulw` or `watch-pr`. The subject is short, imperative, and names a real symbol when one carries the change, for example `fix(ulw): retarget babysit trigger`.
5. **Body.** A one-minute briefing for a reviewer who has the diff: why the change exists, what it leaves out, what it could break, how you proved it works. Short simple sentences, few identifiers, no walls of text. The body becomes the squash commit body, so keep it under about 40 lines. Use `##` headings in this order and drop a section with nothing to say:
   - `## Why`: open with the owner's goal (the one restated in the briefs), then the problem and approach, 1 to 3 short sentences in all. No SHAs, rebase genealogy, or "based on main" preamble.
   - `## What changed`: 1 to 3 short bullets. Name a real symbol or path only when it carries the change. Name both sides of a rename or retarget.
   - `## Scope`: always. 1 to 3 short items on what it covers and what it deliberately leaves out. No symbols, paths, or file-by-file essay.
   - `## Tradeoffs`: only rejected alternatives a reviewer would otherwise ask about.
   - `## Blast Radius`: 1 to 2 sentences on who or what it touches and why that is safe or risky. If trunk is red, state the cost of leaving it red.
   - `## Verification`: 1 to 3 bullets, each a real run path and its outcome. Perf: one primary number with its unit, `before → after`, and a link to the arena or swarm directory for the rest.

   After the sections, attach videos or screenshots when they prove a claim. Full SHAs, swarm or arena lane recitals, lever-correction essays, file-by-file checklists, and "CLEAN" verdicts go in a linked artifact, not the body.
6. **Open it with `gh`, from the main session only.** `gh` is the only forge tool. Write the body to a file and pass it with `--body-file`, never inline text. Push the branch, then `gh pr create --base <trunk or parent branch> --title "<title>" --body-file <file>`. Omit `--draft`: open every PR ready. If one still opens as a draft, run `gh pr ready <number>`. Run `gh pr view <number> --json state,isDraft,baseRefName,headRefOid` before you state any PR status. A worker's brief says "return a patch and the proposed title and body in a file"; it never runs `git push` or `gh`.
7. **Size and stacks.** Prefer five narrow PRs to one large PR. A stack is a base-branch chain. The root PR targets trunk. Each child branch rebases onto its parent's exact tip and its PR targets the parent branch: `gh pr create --base <parent-branch>`, and `gh pr edit <pr> --base <parent-branch>` to retarget. As a parent merges, move its child onto trunk per "Land bottom-up" in `skill://ulw/playbooks/shipping.md`. Branch from trunk only for independent work. Rebase on trunk before substantial stack work. Publish a rebased branch only from the main session, with `git push --force-with-lease=<branch>:<last-pushed-sha>`.
8. **Opening a PR does not start a babysit.** Report the URL to the owner and keep building. Finish the phase or stack first. Run `skill://ulw/playbooks/babysit.md` only when the owner asks for it after the whole stack exists, or when `skill://ulw/playbooks/autopilot-stack.md` or `skill://ulw/playbooks/autopilot-full.md` assigns it. A babysit per new PR stalls the build and spends checks on commits later waves restart. Push back when review feedback drifts from intent.

Reply. In Korean, plain text: each PR with its URL, base, and title, the verification each body cites, and what stays unpushed or unopened and why.
